title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Seventh edition, Volume 21, Surveying-ZYM - EB.15
text: Weishee pleks, however, means properly a steelyard, as Gesenius defines it, may be doubted. The reason for surpassing it does, seems apparently to rest on the circumstances that _hephele_ in the Arabic (case probably a corruption of _hopplelets_, the definite form of the Hebrew word) is the name of the Arabian weighing instrument of the present day’s and because it was a standard, and is known to have been in long and almost exclusive use in Arabia, and indeed in all Asia, that therefore the related or parents your pheles must choose the steelyard. But this rests on the assumption that the common balance had never been taken by to the Arabians. Job, however, who is shown to have been an illumane Arab, and to have resided in the north of Arabia,"does not use pheles, but _mozanains_," to express the balance \; a word which, as already shown, deines the quantum or condim-armed one, and at that period of course undoubtedly used in Arabia.
